entries.title: Remaining leads from the survey of comparable agent orchestrators (Oct 2026)
entries.body:
Leads borrowed from comparable open-source agent orchestrators, surveyed in October 2026 (first imported from issue #671).
Nothing here is a commitment; these are leads to triage.
The orch checked each against the code on 2026-11-17: ideas lym has built or that proved moot are dropped,
partly built ones name only what is still open, and the eight most worth doing are notes of their own in this project.
Each bullet names its source project and the lym module it would touch.

## Plan validation and concurrency (quarry, Plan-Write, board)

- **Typed scope operations on cards** (foremerge): each scope carries an additive or breaking operation,
  and deterministic rules flag colliding pairs even when files do not overlap.
  Worth comparing against board labels and the alignment gate.
- **Symbol leases between concurrent tasks** (Fusion, ORCH): expiring leases on symbol keys serialize overlapping tasks,
  with a deterministic tie-break; lym keeps overlapping tasks apart by board labels.
- **Commit-time reservation guard** (ntm): a pre-commit hook refuses a commit touching what another task holds; needs leases first.
- **Criterion amendment ledger** (oh-my-claudecode): a card's acceptance text changes only through a recorded amendment in weft.

## Review (burler, Bouncer)

- **Quorum of differently-angled judges** (ccswarm): lym fans out lenses but has no quorum vote for high-risk segments.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's parent orch can be asked to see and veto each Code-Review round and each drift judge ruling
  (`code_review_ask_parent`, `judge_ask_parent`); that is one extra judge, not a quorum.
- **Risk tier by changed paths** (yylo): globs over sensitive paths choose the review depth and the gate scope.

## Engine, recipes and governance (shed, tender, orch, board)

- **Cross-run quarantine** (Bernstein): a task that fails three times across runs is held, unless the failures were the host's.
- **Fork a run from a step with a tree snapshot** (Bernstein): `shed goto` moves the cursor but does not restore the warp tree.
- **Warm retry guarded by a workspace hash** (Bernstein): resume the native session only when the tree is unchanged.
- **Evidence reuse by input identity** (yylo): verify is skipped on the same tree; a changed review prompt could rerun only the review.
- **Guidance at the next step boundary** (Conductor): a queue of operator guidance for the next producer's prompt.
  Partly met since 2026-11-19: `notify_parent_on` in `loom.yaml` mails the run's parent when a named row is reached,
  so the parent can brief that row's agent as it starts; there is still no queue of guidance lym itself folds into the prompt.
- **Batched operator questions with recorded assumptions** (Spec Kit `/clarify`, Conductor): Discussion-Write asks at most a few ranked questions,
  each with a recommended answer, and records unanswered ones as assumptions.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's autonomous agents put their questions to the run's parent orch, not to the operator in their pane;
  Discussion, which the operator sits in, still asks in its pane, so this lead concerns Discussion only.
- **Rate-limit wait**: the orch watcher wakes the orch after a usage reset; tender itself schedules no resume.
- **Standing goals and scheduled routines** (ORCH, CAO, Fusion): periodic triage, dependency bumps or `selfreport` sweeps.

## Agent sessions (reed, shuttle)

- **Waiting-for-input signal** (agent-of-empires): shuttle has an awaiting-input state; screen heuristics still decide readiness and startup.
- **Reference status patterns and a paste pitfall** (CAO): compare its regexes and its tmux bracketed-paste note with shuttle's readiness and creel inject.
- **Context forecasting** (ntm): the orch cycles its context; Webster's Master and the loom driver do not, and nothing forecasts.
- **Staggered spawns** (ntm): space Webster forks and batten fan-out by learned rate limits.

## Observability (report, weft)

- **Hash-chained run journal** (Bernstein): a hash chain over producer outputs makes an archived run self-verifying.
- **Unverified-completion rate** (Bernstein): a `lym report` view of completions with no test or gate behind them.
- **Commit-to-record links** (AgentNote): weft links to warp by a `Warp-SHA:` trailer; a note or trailer on each warp commit could link back.
- **Run diff** (ccswarm): `lym report` comparing two archived runs' timelines and token use.
- **OpenTelemetry spans per producer** (Conductor).

## Operator attention (orch, dobby, reed)

- **Attention feed with acknowledgement states** (ntm): dobby's wait reminders have no seen, snoozed or acknowledged states.

## Discussion review (Discussion-Write, stencils, pattern)

- **Requirements-quality checklist** (Spec Kit `/checklist`): items with IDs the Discussion-review judge answers one by one.
- **Fixed analysis categories** (Kiro): inconsistency, ambiguity, conflicts, unstated assumptions and missing edge cases as named lenses.
- **PATTERN rules handed to reviewers** (Spec Kit constitution): its rules as numbered MUSTs in plan and code review prompts.
- **Glob-scoped steering** (Kiro): stencils pull per-area guidance chosen by the paths of a plan's glyphs.

entries.title: A closed area for lym: bwrap sandbox in stages, off by default
entries.brief: Run the lym process tree in a bwrap area with a host proxy and broker, built in three stages with a stop; to be split if it goes ahead
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-10-30)

Every agent lym starts runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, which many people do not accept, and a repository that states it supports safe sandboxing is worth more than one that does not.
The operator uses lym alone, on Linux (OSL-1046: Ubuntu 24.04; Neve: Kubuntu on Ubuntu 26.04, Plasma 6), and has no interest in other users or in Windows.
The research is `docs/research/platform/sandboxing-options-2026-10-30.md`: it weighs `bwrap`, Landlock, a dedicated Linux user, systemd sandboxing, podman and Claude Code's own `/sandbox`, and the packages and cards each would change.

Two exposures hold today with no area: an agent can reach `/run/user/<uid>/bus` and through it `systemd-run --user`, which starts any process outside lym's tree, and it can type into other hubs' tmux panes through their sockets in `/tmp/tmux-<uid>`, the Models hub's among them.

## Idea

Run the whole lym process tree inside a `bwrap` area launched by lym itself, with the agents free inside it and a short, controlled list of exits.
It is an option the operator turns on, never a requirement: with it off, everything works as it does today, and with it on, nothing starts when the sandbox cannot.
The operator thinks the full design is complicated and error-prone, and doubts it will work without large problems, so it is built in stages with a stop between them.
This is one large note and is split into tasks, or a project, only when the operator decides it goes ahead.

### Before the area: two cheap steps

- Start a hub's tmux server from a Konsole window, not a VS Code terminal: the server inherits the `vscode` AppArmor profile, which grants user namespaces to every agent of the hub.
- A line in `README.md` that every agent lym starts runs with bypass permissions, and that lym belongs on a machine the operator is willing to hand to its agents.

### Stage 1: the filesystem area only

`bwrap` with `--unshare-all --die-with-parent --clearenv` around reed's tmux server and everything under it, started by a new `lym area start` and a supervisor inside.

- The hub is bound read-write at its own path, since the tmux server name, the creel socket name, git's worktree links and Claude Code's transcript directory all derive from absolute paths; `/usr`, `/etc` and `/opt` are read-only, `$HOME` a tmpfs with read-only binds of the Go toolchain, the Claude Code binary and the installed `lym`.
- The area has its own Claude config directory and Go caches bound at the usual paths, with the host's plugin cache read-only on top, so the host's `settings.json` hooks never run in it.
- One host directory holds the tmux socket directory, so `lym reed attach` from outside drives the server inside; tried on OSL-1046 with a tmux server inside `bwrap`.
- `.git/hooks` is read-only; `.git/config` was to stay writable for `branch.<b>.lymLocal`, but `fabric-remote-async` removed that mark and `internal/gitrepo/branchmark.go`, so the reason is gone; whether git itself or another lym writer still needs `.git/config` writable is unchecked.
- Network stays open and there is no broker, so the landing deploy, `lym reed window`, `lym ide` and `lym hibernate request` do not work from inside; the operator does them by hand, from outside.
- A config module `area` with `required`, off by default; `lym area start` refuses on any failure and never falls back to an unsandboxed start.
- Ubuntu 24.04 needs a one-time AppArmor profile for `/usr/bin/bwrap`, loaded by root; the report names the profile, and Ubuntu 25.04 and later ship it, which is not verified on Neve.

This closes the two exposures above and shows early whether tmux, creel and dobby run well inside an area.

### Stop: the operator decides whether stage 1 works well enough to go on.

### Stage 2: egress through a host proxy

No network inside the area; a host-side proxy, reached through a bound socket, allows CONNECT to `api.anthropic.com`, `claude.ai`, `platform.claude.com`, `proxy.golang.org`, `sum.golang.org`, `github.com` and `api.github.com`, with a loopback relay inside the area.
Telemetry and the auto-updater are off by environment.
The GitHub token handed to the area is fine-grained and limited to the hub's repositories; the operator's `gh` login never enters.
WebFetch and the `prowler` skill reach only these hosts.

### Stage 3: a broker for the remaining exits

A host-side process serving a fixed set of verbs and never a command line from the area: the landing deploy (it fetches `origin/main` into its own clone, checks the commit is the tip, builds with the host's Go and installs), `lym reed window` opening Konsole, and `lym hibernate request`.
`lym ide` is refused, since VS Code on the host would run git over repositories the area writes; the host runs no git over the area's repositories at all.

## What is not claimed

Isolation from a kernel exploit, which needs a virtual machine; that data in the area cannot leave through an allowed host; and that a landed change of lym itself cannot run on the host once deployed, which matters on this hub because it develops lym.
Landlock stays a possible inner layer once both machines run a kernel with ABI 9 and 10, and Claude Code deny rules in shuttle's settings are a cheap second line inside the area; the dedicated user, podman, systemd sandboxing and Claude Code's `/sandbox` inside lym runs are left out.
The report estimates the whole at five tasks and eighteen cards.

## Related

Note `creel-cross-hub-mail`: the inbox folder sits outside an area, so reading and writing it goes through the broker.

entries.title: Measure what Cortex XDR costs the test suites on OSL-1046
entries.brief: The 242 s fabricengine tier 1 against 37 to 41 s elsewhere is a machine difference no report has split
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-11-09)

Cortex XDR on OSL-1046 holds each new binary for about 10 s and scans each file a test creates, and fabricengine tests create many.
The shard report (`docs/research/speed/fabricengine-shards-2026-11-09/report.md`) put the 242 s one-process wall down to load, but the 2026-11-08 figure of 37 to 41 s was measured on another machine, so the gap is machine and Cortex, not load.
The package used 1.23 cores of 16 and `pmd` and `piud` were busy in nearly every sample.

## Idea

Separate the Cortex cost from the rest: the time a freshly built test binary waits before it runs, the time file creation takes with and without a scanned folder, and the fabricengine tier 1 wall with the repository and temp folders excluded from the scan, if the operator can have that changed.
The result says whether to cut tests, cut file and binary creation, or ask for an exclusion.

entries.title: Move a running task by hand-back and a fresh run, not a re-parent verb
entries.brief: The writer hands back what it knows, the run is cancelled, a new task under the new parent starts from that
entries.body:
## Seen

The study `docs/research/loom/reparent-running-task-2026-11-12.md` (commit `5e41ee2b`) finds that a verb moving a running task to another parent is feasible but wide:
two durable stores written by two modules with no atomic change, a narrow board write past the run lock,
an ancestry check on the new parent, and a cross-module tapestry run of its own.

## Idea (operator, 2026-11-15)

Moving a running task is rare, and a verb for it is clumsy for what it buys.
Instead, end the run and start a new one with more information:

1. The run's live writer writes everything it has learned to a hand-back file in its run records:
   what is done, the decisions taken, what is left, and where its commits are.
   The entry is held by the run and takes no body edit, so the file is the only place it can write.
2. The run is cancelled with `lym batten cancel`, which sets the entry back to `draft` and frees it.
   The archive tag keeps the run records, the hand-back and the commits, so the new run can read them.
3. The orch writes the hand-back into the entry's body, or into a new task under the new parent, and releases it.

What the design must settle:

- Whether the new run re-uses the old commits (a cherry-pick, which brings back the study's ancestry question) or only reads them.
- Whether this is a recipe step, a `lym batten` verb, or orch guidance alone.

The adopt redesign (`adopt-redesign`) has landed, and so has `run-fsm-tracked-records` (`27eefef6`, one run FSM over tracked records).
The project `adopt-build-resplit` has landed whole: its members `transition-push-takeover`, `machine-registry-holds-catchup`, `adopt-foreground` and `leftover-pairs-teardown` are in (`71d6ee1a`),
so the adopt work this note waited on is built.

entries.title: Code cleanup: cut and simplify lym code and tests
entries.brief: Make lym smaller without changing behaviour: fewer tests, leaner design, no dead compatibility code, no unused features
entries.body:
Make lym smaller without changing what it does, one mechanical pass at a time.

Background: `docs/research/rewrite/shrink-estimate-2026-11-18/report.md` found almost no copy-paste duplication (under 1 %).
The size sits in tests (about 2 test lines per code line), comments,
near-identical helpers a duplicate detector misses, design that makes every caller handle more than it needs,
compatibility and migration code, and features nobody uses.
A clean-room rewrite was judged too large for the gain (2026-11-18); this project cuts in place instead.

## Order

Decided by the operator, 2026-11-19:

1. `drop-compat-migration-code` first, once the single-repo tasks and `hardener-campaign` have landed, since they change the same packages.
2. `doc-go-trim-pass` last, so it trims docs that describe the code after the pass above.

`design-simplify-callers` was dropped (operator, 2026-11-19): its `landingshed-design-simplify` pilot saved 278 lines against an estimate of 600–800.

entries.title: Remove compatibility and migration code no hub needs any more
entries.brief: Retired names, key renames and one-off data migrations still in the code; keep the cheap refusals that point to the new name, delete the rest
entries.body:
## What was seen

Outside tests, "retired" appears in 127 files, "migrat" in 57 and "legacy" in 65 (2026-11-18);
`fabricengine` leads with 18 files, then `loomcli` 11 and `boardengine` 10.
Some of it is a deliberate refusal of an old name or key with a pointer to the new one, which is cheap and stays.
Some is real migration code: `landingshed` alone carries about 100 lines (the retired `Merge-In` row name,
a scratch-to-records attempt migration, a key-rename migration).

## Idea

A mechanical pass, module by module: classify each hit as a refusal (keep) or a migration or compatibility path
whose data no hub still holds (delete).

## Decided

- All migration code goes: the operator confirmed no hub needs it (operator, 2026-11-19).
- `lym board retire-legacy` is part of it: a one-off migration of `tasks.json` and `notes.json` into `board.json` that every hub has run.

entries.title: Trim every package doc.go of what is superfluous
entries.brief: The comment rewrite did not shrink doc.go files (27,301 lines); cut what is superfluous in all of them, fanned out over many small Sonnet agents
entries.body:
## What was measured (2026-11-18, `comment-trim-second-pass`)

Production code has 103,762 comment lines against 268,614 code lines, a 27.9 % share.
The package `doc.go` files hold 27,301 of those comment lines; the comment rewrite last week did not shrink them.
Largest: `fabricengine` 2,474, `websterengine` 1,284, `gatecli` 1,273, `reedengine` 1,174, `shuttleengine` 1,075.
The full measurement is in the change description of that run, records commit `e1d2be8076` in `loomyard-weft`.

## Operator decision (2026-11-18)

Cut everything superfluous in every `doc.go`, not in a chosen set of packages.
Superfluous: text that restates the function or type docs, narrates how the code works step by step, repeats itself, or records history.
What stays: a short package overview, the package's contracts and invariants, and a "why" where the code alone does not show it.

## How the work is done (operator, 2026-11-18)

The writer fans the work out over many Agent-tool subagents on Sonnet at medium effort, each given a fixed small number of `doc.go` files,
so no subagent's context grows large.
The writer sets the batch size by file length, splits the largest files (`fabricengine`, `websterengine`, `gatecli`) into a batch of their own,
and checks each subagent's diff before committing.
No code changes; comments in other files are out of scope.

entries.title: Unjudged red-first refusal burns the verify attempts before the parent answers
entries.body:
## Seen

2026-11-21, in `gate-dotnet-fixes` and `red-first-overlay-non-go-files`: the darn writer asked the parent for a "No test seam" decision, then re-ran the verify gate at once.
The unjudged red-first refusal repeated, the run spent its three verify attempts within about two minutes and stopped with a question,
while the parent's `lym loom decision add` was still committing. The parent then had to resume the run by hand.

## Idea

An unjudged red-first refusal (exit `RedFirstUnjudgedExit`) does not spend a verify attempt; the writer waits for the parent's reply,
or the gate waits for the decision record to change before it re-runs.


## From issue #173

Imported from [issue #173](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/173).

**What happened.**
Darn-Write halted blocked (anomaly escalation-to-human) after the chair's `lym gate red-first --gate darn-write` failed 3 attempts in a row with the same error.
The error: the diff changes a contracts spec markdown file, which the overlay cannot put back, so the base run cannot judge the tests.
The refusal's way forward is for the run's parent to record a `lym loom decision add` entry titled "No test seam".

**Why abnormal.**
The agent receiving the findings cannot resolve this itself; it needs a parent decision.
The gate re-prompted the agent three times, so the whole verify budget went on an identical, deterministic refusal, and the run ended blocked.
A diff that pairs a Go test with a doc update is ordinary; the gate treats the doc as making the whole check unjudgeable.

**What to do.**
Make the red-first check ignore non-Go doc files that cannot affect test outcomes, or restore only the Go files on the base.
When it must refuse, escalate to the parent on the first attempt instead of re-prompting the agent through the full budget with an unactionable finding.

Provenance: task raddle-slug-length-check; note loom-halt.md.

entries.title: One-repository sandbox: create the repo and clone the hub
entries.brief: Create a private sandbox repo with gh, clone it as a one-repository hub, check refs on origin
entries.body:
## Goal

First of three trials of the one-repository hub layout (57015a52) in a new sandbox, driven from this task's worktree; the run acts as the sandbox's operator and orch.

## Steps, exact cap

- Create one private GitHub repository `Knatte18/lym-sandbox-onerepo` with `gh repo create --private` (operator approved, 2026-11-21), seeded with a tiny Go module (one package, one test) on `main`.
- Clone it once as a one-repository hub with `lym fabric clone --single-repo` under `/home/knatte/Code/lym-sandbox-onerepo-LYMHUB`.
- Check and record: `gh api` branch and tag lists show only the code branch; `git ls-remote` shows the board and prime records branch under `refs/lym/heads/`; `lym board list` and `lym fabric` status work in the hub.
- No other repository is created; nothing is deleted.

## Output

A report under `docs/research/single-repo/sandbox-1-setup-2026-11-21/report.md`: each command, its outcome and every friction or failure.
Each lym bug found is filed as a note on this hub's board (kind note, labels from `lym board labels`).

entries.title: One-repository sandbox: run tasks to landing
entries.brief: Run sequential, concurrent and abandoned tasks in the sandbox hub and check origin after each
entries.body:
## Goal

Second trial: run real tasks in the one-repository sandbox hub that the setup trial created (`/home/knatte/Code/lym-sandbox-onerepo-LYMHUB`).

## Steps, exact cap

- File three small tasks on the sandbox board, each a few lines of Go in the seed module, recipe darn, profile light, writer opus medium.
- Run the first two one after the other to landing; run the third alongside a fourth trivial task, so two runs are in flight at once.
- Start one more trivial task and abandon it: remove its pair and board entry.
- After each landing and the abandon, record on origin: records branches and archive tags under `refs/lym/`, the board, and the code branch list GitHub shows.
- Cap: at most five sandbox runs in total; no repeats.

## Output

A report under `docs/research/single-repo/sandbox-2-tasks-2026-11-21/report.md`, with each lym bug filed as a note on this hub's board.

entries.title: One-repository sandbox: second clone and namespace hand check
entries.brief: Clone the sandbox again, land a task from it, and grep fabric and gitrepo for un-namespaced records refs
entries.body:
## Goal

Third trial: a fresh clone of the sandbox hub and the hand check the one-repository landing (57015a52) left open.

## Steps, exact cap

- Clone `Knatte18/lym-sandbox-onerepo` once more, into a second hub directory, with plain `lym fabric clone <url>`; check it detects the one-repository layout and shows the board and the landed tasks' records.
- Run one small task to landing from the second clone, then pull in the first hub and check it sees that landing.
- Hand check from the landing commit: grep `internal/fabric*` and `internal/gitrepo` for origin ref names built from a bare `refs/heads/` or `refs/tags/` string on a records-store path; list each site and whether it is wrong.

## Output

A report under `docs/research/single-repo/sandbox-3-reclone-2026-11-21/report.md` that also sums up all three trials; each lym bug filed as a note on this hub's board.

entries.title: Plan amendment to an unchanged card is approved without being carried into it
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #168](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/168).

## Seen

On a tapestry run in Webster, the parent recorded `lym loom decision add <slug> --by parent --amends-plan` naming a concrete change to one card (new Edit targets and a changed Intent), then ran `lym loom goto --to Plan-Burler-Review` and `lym loom resume`.
Plan-Burler-Review approved in one round without editing the card.
Its review said the amendment was not carried into the card, but that "the round's check admits a new finding only on a changed hunk in a file the changes file lists", and the changes file listed only `00-overview.md` from an earlier amendment round.
Webster then began the batch again, its fork stopped on the unamended card, and the run blocked at Webster.
An earlier amendment on the same run, which added new cards, did go through the same path.

## Workaround

A second parent decision, without `--amends-plan`, told Webster that the batch's fork follows the amending decision over the card, editing the extra targets, and records the batch without a plan edit.
Then `lym loom resume`.

## Expected

An `--amends-plan` decision routed to `amendment_target` lets the plan review raise findings on the cards the amendment names, even when those cards have no changed hunk, so the fixer edits them.


## From issue #170

Imported from [issue #170](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/170).

## What happened

A Webster row that finds a begun batch waiting on a plan edit halts as `blocked` and sends the run back to `Plan-Burler-Review`.
Over one run this round trip repeated five times (`Webster` stuck, `Plan-Burler-Review` goto, review stuck, `Plan-Burler-Fix` stuck, `Plan-Bouncer` done, `Drift-Await`/`Drift-Expect` skipped, `Webster` stuck again).
Each time the Webster halt reason asked for a concrete plan edit, and the next Webster halt asked for an edit again:

- One halt asked for card 14 to list three additional targets. After a full review/fix/bouncer pass, the next halt asked for the same amendment, naming "plan fixer or `lym webster rebaseline --card 14`" as the way forward.
- A later halt asked for a re-sign arrow head in card 15 to be corrected, then `lym webster rebaseline --card 15` run.
  `lym webster record-batch 14` had refused with `resign-not-done/15-dp-heuristic-full-size[blocking]` and pointed to `lym webster recover-batch 14`.
- One halt came from the auto-rebaseline guard: `00-overview.md changed outside its Card Index`, with the way forward "restore 00-overview.md, or fix the plan".

The history shows `Plan-Burler-Fix` recorded as `stuck` and `Plan-Bouncer` as `done` in the passes that followed, with no sign the requested edit was made.

## Why it is abnormal

The review/fix/bouncer pass completes without acting on the edit Webster asked for, and Webster does not pass its halt reason to the plan fixer as a required change.
Each unresolved request costs a full plan-review pass plus an operator or parent intervention, and the loop only ends when a parent edits the plan by hand.

## What to do

- Hand the Webster halt reason to `Plan-Burler-Review` and `Plan-Burler-Fix` as a finding that must be resolved, and refuse `Plan-Bouncer` done while that finding stands.
- Where the way forward is a `lym webster rebaseline --card N` call, let the loop run it after the fix instead of halting on it.

## Provenance

Task `lagrangian-gap-measurement`; notes `loom-halt-2.md`, `loom-halt-3.md`, `loom-halt-4.md`, `loom-halt-5.md`, `loom-halt-6.md`, `loom-halt.md`, `webster-refusal-record-batch.md`.

entries.title: webster: halt note truncates drift gate message; no way to accept expected drift
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #172](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/172).

## What happened

A run halted `blocked` at Webster (anomaly `escalation-to-human`) after the plan changed and was rebaselined on entry, keeping 1 begun batch.
The verify gate then failed: "verify gate did not pass after 3 of 3 re-prompt(s): the run-level "drift" entry failed: unexpected cell: changed in case ...".
The drift findings were numeric cells in a captured baseline file that moved in the sixth significant digit (for example an integer value changing in its last digits and a rate changing in its last decimal).
The halt note's message is cut off mid-finding, in the middle of a quoted value, and the way-forward text ("1) fix what the "drift" entry's findings name and commit it on the task branch; 2) re-step the Webster row") is cut off after step 2.

## Why it is abnormal

1. The halt note truncates the gate message, so the full list of drifted cells and the complete way forward are not in the note.
2. Drift in the last digits of a captured numeric baseline is the shape of a legitimate behaviour change from the card's own work.
   Three re-prompts of the implementing agent cannot "fix" it, and the way forward offers no route to accept it as expected.
   The gate looped to its re-prompt limit on a finding that needs an operator or parent decision.

## What to do

- Stop truncating the halt note's message, or write the full gate report to a file under the friction directory and name it in the note.
- Offer an explicit way to accept an expected drift (for example a re-baseline verb for the "drift" entry), and say so in the way forward.
- Consider ending the re-prompt loop early when the same drift findings come back unchanged after a re-prompt.

Provenance: task `wemod-invariants`; note `loom-halt-2.md`.

entries.title: Burler-fix halts failed when a fork runs git in a scratch repo under .scratch
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #177](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/177).

What happened: loom halted `failed` at Plan-Burler-Fix (anomaly `producer-hard-failure`, round 1 attempt 1).
The reason: the twill fixer fork ran a git-mutating command and the guard refused it with "a fork must never run a state-mutating git command".
The command created a throwaway probe directory under the worktree's `.scratch/`, ran `git init` for a bare repo and a work repo there, committed to the work repo, and pushed to the bare repo with `--force-with-lease`.
It never touched the task repository's own refs or working tree.
The fork was probing git push behaviour for a finding.

Why abnormal: the guard treats any `git init`, `commit` or `push` as mutating, including against a repo the fork created inside its own scratch directory.
The way forward it names ("inspect the target's working-tree changes, revert what the fork wrote") has nothing to revert here, so a harmless probe ends a run as hard failure.

What to do: scope the mutating-git check to the target repository and its remotes.
Allow git commands whose repo is a directory under `.scratch/`, or, if forks must not run them at all, say so in the fork prompt and give forks a sanctioned way to probe git behaviour.
Also make the halt message say when no target change was found.

Provenance: task single-repo-namespace-layout; notes loom-halt.md.

entries.title: Burler fixer step re-runs on a round an earlier fixer finished, with no reason in the prompt
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #176](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/176).

What happened: the Plan-Burler-Fix step for round 1 started a fixer session after an earlier fixer session had already fixed every finding and run its self-check.
The earlier fixer's report sat under a timestamped name (`round-1-fixer-report-<UTC timestamp>.md`) rather than the expected `round-1-fixer-report.md`.
The prompt gave no reason for the second run, so the fixer had to read every card to tell "re-run because the report was misnamed or rejected" from "re-run for new work".
It wrote the expected report from the earlier dispositions and spawned no forks.

Why abnormal: the step's report-name expectation and the name the first fixer wrote disagree, so a finished round looks unfinished and costs a full fixer session.
The prompt also never states why a step runs again.

What to do: find why the first fixer's report landed under the timestamped name and was not accepted as the round's report (archiving on write, or a name mismatch).
Either accept the archived report, or state the re-run reason (misnamed or rejected report versus new work) in the fixer prompt.

Provenance: task single-repo-namespace-layout; notes burler-plan-r1.md.

entries.title: loom-halt note and blocked reason name a gate-findings path that does not exist
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #174](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/174).

Import note: the issue names files under `.lym/`, which is deleted with its worktree, so only what the issue quotes of them reached the board: `.lym/shed/`, `.lym/shuttle/`.

**What happened.**
The halt reason for a Darn-Write gate failure says "findings:" followed by a path under `.lym/shed/<slug>/gate-findings/Darn-Write.md`.
That file does not exist; the `.lym/shed/<slug>` directory is empty.
The trace log names a different path, `.lym/shuttle/<run>/gate-findings.md`, and that run directory is gone too.

**Why abnormal.**
The halt note and the `lym loom resume` way forward point the operator at findings that cannot be read.
The cause of the block is only recoverable from the trace log.

**What to do.**
Copy the findings file to the stable path the halt reason names before the shuttle run directory is removed, or name the path that survives.

Provenance: task raddle-slug-length-check; note loom-halt.md.

entries.title: loom pr-findings fails in PR-Review: NewParentAlign Deps.OpenFabric must not be nil
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #169](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/169).

`lym loom pr-findings <file>` fails in a PR-Review session on a well-formed findings file, every time, so the parent's findings cannot be routed.

## Where

A PR-Review agent, the session spawned for a task's pull request after its landing opened it.
The parent orch sent two findings by creel; the agent wrote them in burler's review format under `.scratch/` and ran `lym loom pr-findings .scratch/parent-review-1.md`.

## What happens

The file passes burler's format check (a first attempt with a wrong verdict was refused with a clear message, and the corrected file got past that check).
The verb then fails reading the send-back edge:

```
{"error":"loom: pr-findings: read whether the send-back edge can fire: loomrecipe: shedbuild: producer 16 \"Parent-Align\": shedrecipe: ParentAlign: landingshed: NewParentAlign: Deps.OpenFabric must not be nil; way forward: run lym loom pr-findings .scratch/parent-review-1.md again, and tell the operator when it keeps failing","ok":false}
```

Running it again gives the same error.

## Expected

The verb answers send-back or fix-here.
`NewParentAlign` looks to be built on this path without its `OpenFabric` dependency.

## Workaround

The operator told the agent to fix the findings directly, bypassing the verb.

entries.title: webster: Create check ignores a decision that drops the Create; recover-batch advised anyway
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #171](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/171).

## What happened

Batch 01 of a four-card batch failed `lym webster record-batch 01` and then `lym webster recover-batch 01` with the same `create-not-done[blocking]` finding: a card's Create target did not resolve (quarry answered `not_found`, "the unit exists and the member is missing").
The run's parent had recorded a decision (`lym loom decision add`) that drops that Create, so the member is meant never to exist.
Both refusals still gave the generic way forward: "recover-batch 01 to build the target as the card names it", or amend the card's Create target and run `lym webster rebaseline --card NN`.
The run then halted `blocked` at Webster (anomaly `escalation-to-human`) with the note "the parent's decision drops that Create, so card 1 needs a plan amendment".

## Why it is abnormal

The verifier checks the card's Create target against the worktree and ignores the recorded decision that drops it.
`recover-batch` is advised although it can only rebuild what the card names, which the decision forbids.
The refusal does not tell the operator or parent that a dropped Create needs a card amendment and rebaseline, nor does it say whether the decision record can retire the Create finding.
The result is a halt on a state the parent already resolved.

## What to do

- Make the Create check read the run's decision record and treat a Create dropped by a decision as satisfied, or report it as "dropped by decision" rather than `blocking`.
- When a finding matches a dropped Create, make the way forward name the card amendment plus `lym webster rebaseline --card NN` and not offer `recover-batch` as the first option.

Provenance: task `wemod-invariants`; notes `loom-halt.md`, `webster-refusal-record-batch.md`, `webster-refusal-recover-batch.md`.


## From issue #178

Imported from [issue #178](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/178).

What happened: Webster halted `blocked` (anomaly `escalation-to-human`) on the first batch.
`lym webster record-batch 01` and then `lym webster recover-batch 01` both refused with `batch_failed` and `create-not-done[blocking]`: a card's Create target still did not resolve, and quarry answered `not_found` (the unit exists, the member is missing).
The halt message says the batch's fork had reverted the work under a decision the parent had since superseded; the parent's later decision (#2210) reverses it.
So the fork built against a stale decision although a newer one was on record.

Two lym defects show here:
1. The implementer fork was not given, or did not weigh, a later parent decision that supersedes an earlier one.
   Decision precedence (the later entry wins) does not reach the fork, so the batch fails and the run escalates to the operator.
2. The two refusals give different way-forward text for the same finding.
   `record-batch` offers two paths: `recover-batch` to build the target as the card names it, or amend the card, run `lym webster rebaseline --card NN`, then `recover-batch`.
   `recover-batch` offers only the amend-and-rebaseline path.
   Here the right fix was to build the target as the card names it, which `recover-batch` does not offer; the missing option is misleading for a re-run that is itself the recovery.

What to do: make the batch fork's prompt carry the decision record with later entries marked as overriding earlier ones, and have the batch check flag a fork whose output contradicts a superseding decision.
Make `recover-batch` list the same way-forward options as `record-batch`, or say why it omits the build-as-named path.

Provenance: task single-repo-namespace-layout; notes loom-halt-2.md, webster-refusal-record-batch.md, webster-refusal-recover-batch.md.

entries.title: Stencil build-version refusal at Preflight appends an inapplicable config/model-spec way forward
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #175](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/175).

A loom run halted `blocked` at Preflight because the stencil store refused a stencil written by a newer lym build than the running one.

The refusal text ends with two way-forward clauses:

```
way forward: restart the run's driver on the current lym binary, and update that binary first if it is older than the board; way forward: fix the config or model spec it names, then re-step
```

The first clause is correct for this cause.
The second is a generic suffix that the halt path appends, and it does not apply: no config or model spec is named, and the cause is a stale binary.
Following it sends the operator to look for a config fault that does not exist.

The halt anomaly was `escalation-to-human`, and the run history holds a single `Preflight / stuck` entry.

Expected: a build-version refusal from `stencilstore` carries only its own way forward, without the generic config/model-spec suffix.

Full error as recorded:

```
seat stencils check failed: build the darn writer table: darn: DarnTable: Step 4 list: stencilstore: stencil "darn-fragment-make-change-gated" was written by lym build fded58794f7b02939b6bf8675b87c64fb3fa987d, which is newer than the running build 4c031f8b7a781e3f4fb17f48632782ded92f3a01, and this process may not render it
```

Provenance: task `bugfix-discussion-stencil`, from `loom-halt.md`.
